name: PPFN Advanced KSampler (BrownianTree hijack blend)
plain: Replaces the core Brownian tree sampler class during sampling with one that nudges the Brownian tree result toward a blend with power-law, Perlin, or cross-hatch noise. A way of getting any of those noises into SDE samplers. The nudge is small, 3% of the blend difference, and sigma tolerance scales the blend factor; 0 turns it off.
math:
Patch class comfy.k_diffusion.sampling.BrownianTreeNoiseSampler with PNSNoiseSampler.
sample_noise: tree = W(Δ)/√|Δt|. If sigma_tol=0, returns tree.
s=((σ−σmin)/(σmax/2−σmin))·tol/2; boost_leading_sigma: s×1.25, capped at 1, while noise_idx<steps//4.
No guide: out = tree ± 0.03·(blend(tree, sharpen(noise,.5), s) − tree), + when additive.
label: from code
surprise: Hijacks the sampler class in module scope, not a noise_sampler argument, so it affects any SDE sampler during that run. Blend weight is a fixed 0.03 in the additive and subtractive branches.

audit.note: nodes.py:733-736 and the blend after it: the result is tree ± 0.03·(blend(tree, sharpen(noise,0.5), s) − tree), so only 3% of the blend difference is added, with a sign set by noise_mode. sigma_tol scales the blend factor; it does not control where the blend applies.
